description: Language-agnostic rules: transport security, disabled protections, debug exposure, weak algorithms.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.remediation: Disabling verification makes the connection trivially interceptable - encryption without authentication is not security. Point the client at the correct CA bundle instead.

rules.title: Cleartext HTTP used for an API or auth endpoint
rules.remediation: Use https. Cleartext credentials and tokens are readable by anything on the path, including the coffee-shop Wi-Fi.

rules.title: Authentication or authorization disabled by a flag
rules.remediation: Confirm this is not reachable in production. Auth toggles intended for local development have a habit of shipping enabled, and this is one of the most commonly exploited misconfigurations there is.

rules.title: Debug mode enabled
rules.remediation: Debug mode typically exposes stack traces, environment variables, and in Flask/Werkzeug an interactive console that executes arbitrary Python. Drive it from an environment variable that defaults to off.

rules.title: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to a wildcard
rules.remediation: Acceptable for genuinely public, unauthenticated data. For anything else, echo a validated origin from an allowlist.

rules.title: JWT algorithm set to none
rules.remediation: alg=none means unsigned - anyone can mint a valid token. Always pass an explicit algorithm allowlist to the verifier.

rules.title: Broken or deprecated cryptographic algorithm
rules.remediation: Use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for encryption and SHA-256+ for hashing. ECB mode leaks plaintext structure regardless of the underlying cipher.

rules.title: Service bound to all network interfaces
rules.remediation: Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the service on every interface, including public ones. Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless it genuinely needs to be reachable externally, and put a firewall in front of it either way.

rules.title: Default or trivially weak credentials
rules.remediation: Default credential pairs are the first thing any scanner or botnet tries. Generate a unique password at provisioning time and require a change on first login.

rules.title: Comment flags an unresolved security concern
rules.remediation: Someone already knew about this. Worth reading before shipping - self-flagged security debt is unusually high-signal.

rules.title: World-writable file mode in code
rules.remediation: Any local user can modify a world-writable file. Use 0o600 for secrets and 0o644 for ordinary data.

rules.title: Client IP taken from an untrusted header
rules.remediation: These headers are attacker-controlled unless a proxy you own overwrites them. If they gate rate limiting, allowlisting, or audit logs, that control is bypassable - trust only the hop count your own proxy sets.

rules.title: Database grant of all privileges
rules.remediation: Grant only the statements the application actually issues. An app account with DROP or GRANT rights turns any SQL injection into total loss.

rules.title: Hostname verification disabled
rules.remediation: Without hostname verification, a valid certificate for any domain is accepted for yours. Keep it on.

rules.title: Symmetric signing secret hardcoded
rules.remediation: Anyone with this value can forge sessions and tokens for every user. Load it from the environment and rotate it - note that rotating invalidates existing sessions.
